correctness.rationale: The primary equations impose \(F_u+F_c=F\), and substituting the published zero-food state gives \(F_u'=p_fF>0\). Eliminating \(F_u=F-F_c\) at the clean-food equilibrium yields the displayed \(3\times3\) infected/environmental block. Its characteristic cubic has constant term \(kd_Bq(1-\mathcal R_F)\). For \(q>0\), \(\mathcal R_F<1\) implies \(a\xi_l<kd_B\); the remaining Routh--Hurwitz inequalities are strictly positive. A fresh symbolic check confirmed the package identity for \(A_1A_2-A_3\). The exact witness gives published \(1/3\), corrected \(4/3\), and cubic \(\lambda^3+5\lambda^2+6\lambda-1\).
risks: The threshold theorem excludes the critical case \(p_f=\alpha_4F\) and is local rather than global.

value.rationale: The correction changes both the existence of the printed disease-free equilibrium and the invasion threshold. An exact positive-parameter witness reverses the source's stability prediction, so this is a substantive model correction rather than a cosmetic normalization issue.

final_claim: In the 2026 ready-to-eat-food listeriosis subsystem, the published zero-food disease-free point is not an equilibrium for positive total food. On the invariant food-total manifold the clean-food equilibrium has local invasion threshold \(\mathcal R_F=\mathcal R_0^L(1+\alpha_3F/(p_f-\alpha_4F))\) when \(p_f>\alpha_4F\); it is locally stable below that threshold and unstable above it.
limitations: Critical \(p_f=\alpha_4F\), endemic equilibria, and global dynamics are outside the claim.
